_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR EVERY IMAGE ON THE SITE.
The website's HTML never references a camera filename. It references the
stable logical IDs below. Swapping in the owner's original high-resolution
photos therefore means editing ONLY this file -- no HTML, CSS or JS change,
and no redesign.
TO SWAP IN AN ORIGINAL HIGH-RES PHOTO:
1. Drop the new file into  assets/incoming/
2. In that image's entry below:  "file": "incoming/<newfile>"
3. Set  "crop": null   (a real original has no letterbox bars to remove)
4. Adjust "focus" if the subject sits somewhere new
5. Run:  npm run images
See docs/swapping-images.md for the full walkthrough.
FIELD REFERENCE
file    Path relative to assets/. Today these point at assets/originals/,
which holds the owner's supplied files byte-for-byte untouched.
group   Output subdirectory under public/img/.
crop    [left, top, right, bottom] in SOURCE-IMAGE pixel coordinates.
Strips the iPhone letterbox bars and, where noted, burned-in
marketing overlays. null = use the whole source.
focus   Focal point as [x, y] fractions, 0..1, of the cropped image.
Becomes `object-position` in the generated image-focus.css, so
the subject stays in frame at every container aspect ratio.
alpha   true -> key the solid black backing plate to transparent and
emit PNG + WebP instead of AVIF/WebP/JPEG (logos only).
formats Override the default avif/webp/jpg set.
usage   Where this image appears. Documentation only.
NOTE ON TODAY'S QUALITY CEILING
Every current source is a 1290x2796 iPhone screenshot whose real content
is a band in the middle. The pipeline NEVER upscales, so output tops out
near 1290px wide. The markup already requests 1600/1920/2560; those rungs
appear automatically the moment a true original is swapped in.
Photographs are served at their natural cropped aspect ratio. Containers
set aspect-ratio and crop with `object-fit: cover`. Pre-cropping to each
container's shape in the pipeline was discarding up to 45% of the width of
sources that cannot spare it.
